topic: GitHub Copilot Usage-Based Billing Guide: Understanding June 2026 Flex Pricing

competitors.title: GitHub Copilot is moving to usage-based billing (Official, Apr 27 2026)
key_points: All Copilot plans transition to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, replacing premium request units (PRUs) with GitHub AI Credits
Base plan pricing unchanged: Pro $10/mo, Pro+ $39/mo, Business $19/user/mo, Enterprise $39/user/mo
Code completions and Next Edit Suggestions remain unlimited on paid plans — do not consume AI Credits
Credits consumed by token usage (input, output, cached tokens) at published API rates per model
Business/Enterprise get pooled included usage across the org and new admin budget controls
Existing Business/Enterprise customers get promotional credits June–August: Business $30/user, Enterprise $70/user
Fallback experiences eliminated — no more automatic downgrade to cheaper model on exhaustion
Code review also consumes GitHub Actions minutes in addition to AI Credits
Annual plan subscribers stay on request-based billing until term expiry, then transition
Preview bill experience launched early May for cost visibility before the switch

competitors.title: GitHub Copilot Usage-Based Billing Explained (June 2026)
key_points: 1 AI Credit = $0.01 USD — token consumption directly maps to credit cost
Copilot Pro: $10/mo includes 1,000 base credits with flex allotment above base
Copilot Pro+: $39/mo includes 3,900 base credits
Copilot Business: $19/user/mo includes 1,900 credits per user, pooled across organization
Copilot Enterprise: $39/user/mo includes 3,900 credits per user, pooled
Promotional amounts June–September 2026: Business 3,000 credits/user, Enterprise 7,000 credits/user
Features consuming credits: Copilot Chat, Agent mode, Code review, CLI, Cloud agents, Spaces
Features NOT consuming credits: Code completions, Next Edit Suggestions (unlimited on paid)
Model choice, prompt size, agentic depth, and review effort determine cost per interaction
Old request-based billing only applies now to existing annual Pro/Pro+ subscribers on legacy plans

competitors.title: GitHub Copilot Flex Billing Backlash Explained (June 2026)
key_points: By June 2, developers reported burning through monthly Pro credit allocations in hours
GitHub Discussions thread #197089 had thousands of replies by June 12
Neither GitHub nor Microsoft had publicly responded to the backlash by June 14
New Copilot Max tier at $100/month with large credit pool introduced for heavy users
Heavy users hitting zero balance in 1–3 days using Claude Opus 4.8 or Fable 5 models
Top 5% of paid Copilot users generating ~60% of inference cost (TechCrunch, May 2026)
Industry-wide shift to metered billing — flat-rate unlimited AI coding ending across the board
Three main complaints: credit depletion faster than promised, weak budget controls, poor communication
Recommendation to audit daily usage and match plan to actual profile — not panic-cancel
Microsoft's June 30 directive ending internal Claude Code licenses added fuel to backlash

competitors.title: GitHub Copilot's Flex Billing Explained (SaaS Master, June 8 2026)
key_points: Prices unchanged but what those dollars buy changed — now a credit allowance, not unlimited usage
Copilot Max: $100/month with 20,000 AI Credits (about $200 of usage value)
Light users likely won't notice change; heavy agent users need to monitor credit burn
Flex billing aligns cost with actual compute — flat fee either overcharges light users or bankrupts provider on heavy ones
Cursor and Devin Desktop still lead with flat tiers, but gap is narrowing — entire industry converging on metered pricing
Three-step checklist: check usage view, estimate burn rate, pick matching tier with headroom

competitors.title: Devs Sound Off on Usage-Based Copilot Pricing Change (Visual Studio Magazine, Apr 27 2026)
key_points: Developers pushed back immediately, saying change makes Copilot less predictable and less valuable
'You will get less, but pay the same price' — core user sentiment
Token-based billing makes usage harder to predict: cost depends on prompt, tools, files, model, output
Users questioned Copilot's value vs direct API consumption — 'effectively becoming a wrapper over API consumption'
Requests for Opus model access restoration tied to new billing model
Rollover questions: unused credits expire at end of billing period — no carryover
Cancellation and refund requests spiked; cancellation option available until May 20 for annual plans
Alternatives mentioned: kilo.ai with 500+ models on OpenRouter, Cursor, Claude Code
'Removing the free models destroys any value in the individual plans'

Promotional credit boost for Business/Enterprise June–September 2026: Business gets $30/user (3,000 credits), Enterprise gets $70/user (7,000 credits)

The GitHub Discussions thread #197089 had thousands of replies by June 12, 2026 with no official GitHub response as of June 14
Top 5% of paid Copilot users generate roughly 60% of inference cost, driving the shift from flat-rate to metered billing
